title: Calibration rings show clearly, but cross arms and images are invisible (Slimtype DS8A5SH, CD-R 80)
body: Setup Disc Image Studio v1.5.0 (win-x64), Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (build 19045) Recorder: Slimtype DVD A DS8A5SH (E:), a laptop slim drive Media: CD-R 80 min, hub code “CD-R 80 CWLHT-1744”. The drive reports 359,846 total and 359,844 usable sectors. Burn method: in-app live streaming burn (IMAPI2 DAO), automatic speed (lowest, 10x / 1.8 MB/s), delayed interleaving on All burns completed without errors (807.1 MiB, about 512 s each) What I tried Image burn, no calibration (Standard 80 min preset, 24.5–56.8 mm; 2 levels, dither 52%, brightness −12): nothing visible on the disc. Coarse calibration target: the six band edges are clearly visible. Marking them along one radius gave an accepted band-edge estimate of 25.28 mm inner / 58.05 mm outer. The app said “The stripes were too weak or the readings disagreed. Only the band-edge estimate is available.” Two earlier marking attempts along other radii were rejected with “A boundary differs by over 0.40 mm”. Image burn with the coarse radii applied to the project (2 levels, dither 77%, brightness +1, sRGB gamma on): still nothing visible at all, not even a smeared shape. Fine calibration target (rings + cross) burned with 25.28–58.05 mm: all 8 rings are clearly visible and concentric. I unwrapped the photo to polar coordinates and the rings come out as flat lines, so the radii look right. But the cross arms are not visible anywhere, not as straight lines and not as curves or spirals, so there is nothing to trace for fine calibration. Questions Is it expected that the rings show but the radial arms don’t on some drives? Could this drive’s write strategy (or the slim drive itself) be unable to produce angular detail? If the arms are smeared by a large angle error, is there another way to get the angle or track-pitch information? For example: a different target, a sector-count or linear-velocity adjustment, or a lighting angle that brings radial features out better? Would exporting WAV+CUE and burning with ImgBurn or cdrecord behave differently from the live IMAPI2 burn on this drive? Attachments Coarse calibration photo (rings visible) Fine calibration photo (rings visible, no arms) Polar-unwrapped version of the fine calibration photo (8 flat ring lines, no slanted or arm features) Calibration records [calibration-3ed954da.calibration.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34544723/calibration-3ed954da.calibration.json) [calibration-8e5d2fc2.calibration.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34544724/calibration-8e5d2fc2.calibration.json) Thanks for the tool. Any pointers appreciated!

title: CMC DVD-R (CMDR47G-CFMWM03): boundary stage stays at 0.45–0.54 mm, fine-cross arms wind too tightly to trace
body: ## Setup - Disc Image Studio v1.4.2 (Windows) - Burner: PIONEER BD-RW BDR-TD05, write speed "Automatic (lowest speed, recommended)", streaming burn - Media: HP DVD-R 16x 4.7 GB, media ID CMDR47G-CFMWM03 (CMC Magnetics), 2,297,888 sectors ## 1. Built-in preset test I burned a test image (12 radial spokes, rings at 32 / 42 / 52 mm, text) with the built-in preset "Verbatim DVD-R AZO (43533) (measured)". The rings appeared at the correct radii. The spokes and the text were not visible at all. Test disc burned with the Verbatim preset: ## 2. Coarse calibration The target was created from the Verbatim preset radii (23.991 / 57.965 mm). All 3 angle marks were read: - Corrected radii: inner 23.950 mm, outer 57.958 mm, 3 angle marks verified - Band estimate: 23.588 / 56.828 mm - Angle offsets per nominal turn (inner / middle / outer): +0.28 / +0.25 / +0.04 degrees Coarse target photo: ## 3. Boundary calibration (WavyBoundary) The target was generated at 23.950238720108224 / 57.95845741522966 mm with the Verbatim pitch coefficients. I traced it several times (7-8 segments, 40-80 points). Every candidate stays at RMS 0.45-0.54 mm (max 1.4-2.5 mm). The app shows two warnings: "segments do not match a single disc model" and "candidates with different winding counts still fit". Boundary target photo: Solve result: The calibration session file is in the attached ZIP. ## 4. Fine calibration (ReferenceCross) I generated the cross from the coarse result. The reference rings are clear. The cross arms are only visible as two short hooks on opposite sides, at roughly r = 49-51 mm. The rest of each arm wraps tightly between the rings and cannot be seen, so the required 12-point / 60% trace is not possible. Fine target photo: Visible parts of the arms (marked): ## Offline checks on the attached boundary session I built DiscImageStudio.Core from the v1.4.2 source and ran CalibrationBoundaryFitter.Fit on the saved session. It gives the same numbers as the app: - All segments, search range 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.05 mm: best RMS 0.488 / 0.538 / 0.538 mm - Leaving out one segment at a time: best RMS 0.316-0.582 mm (no single bad segment) - Adding 12 inner-band edges traced automatically from the rectified photo: best RMS 0.412 mm - Letting the search use other pitch coefficients (linear or quadratic +/-0.001 to +/-0.004): best RMS 0.354 mm - For comparison, the bundled example calibration-3f2ce8c2: best RMS 0.205 mm - Photo rectification: outer edge 2.58 px, hole 0.99 px My guess is that this CMC media has a track-pitch profile that differs from the model more than the radius-only coarse and boundary stages can correct. The unequal coarse offsets (+0.28 / +0.25 / +0.04) point the same way. I could not confirm this. ## Questions 1. Is CMC media (CMDR47G) expected to work, or is it known to be difficult? 2. Is there a recommended workflow when the boundary stage cannot fit? For example, a stage that also fits pitch, a different target, or a way to start the pitch coefficients from the coarse angle offsets. 3. Would you like any other files or photos? title: Getting empty burned disc when calibrating boundary with CD-R
body:
> I went through 4-5 CD-Rs already, trying to get past the first calibration stage, with any other option not bringing any visible result.
> It might be a built in feature to CD-Rs, but I assume (as true in my case), nobody really cares about the CD contents, rather just want a pretty image burned into it.
> Therefore, I believe it would be beneficial if the software would allow to use an already burned CD as blank, to repeat and try different burning settings. That is assuming many of us have and will be getting more empty discs which are not usable anymore until we get the settings right.

My issue was and still is - I get past the Coarse calibration (images below), and get nothing after burning the boundary calibration media (DIS says the burning was successful, and the CD-R may no longer be burned after it).

nodes.body: Re-burning an already recorded CD-R isn't physically possible. Multisession recording can append data to unused space, but it cannot overwrite an existing image.

If you're mainly struggling with calibration, this might help: I've been working on [[disc-probe](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe)](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe), which estimates disc geometry automatically from optical drive read timing and can export presets to DiscImageStudio.

It's been tested on several CD drives, though compatibility varies. CD-R still needs an additional calibration step to resolve an offset that timing alone can't measure, so it's not completely photo-free yet.

It won't let you reuse burned CD-Rs, but it might help reduce the number of discs lost to trial and error.

I figured it was a property of CD-Rs. But I am certain that no "burning" was done, so I would imagine there would be some way to trick the software/burn drive to think it's a blank.

Anyway, I've got 3 wide, crispy bands in the coarse calibration, how come the boundary calibration, nor burning an actual image get any visible result? Am I missing something in the UI? I tried to carefully follow the instructions, exported the settings of the 
"successful" coarse cal, but it seems meaningless in the next steps. Could it be too "poor" of a quality CD?

@Ashley-QwQ Just saw your new comment, will definitely check this out, thanks!

Glad you'll give it a try!

If you can see three clear bands from coarse calibration, that disc was definitely written. For the other discs, though, no visible image doesn't necessarily mean nothing was burned. I'd check the disc status and burn logs before assuming they're still blank.

One thing worth checking in the DIS workflow: according to the calibration docs, you need to apply the coarse calibration result, then create a new boundary calibration target using the updated parameters. For a normal image, you also need to save the applied parameters as a preset and explicitly select it in your project. Exporting the calibration settings alone doesn't automatically update the design project.

Since the coarse bands came out clearly, I wouldn't blame the CD quality just yet.

Could you share your drive model, CD-R type, and whether the later burn jobs completed successfully? A screenshot of the boundary calibration preview and the resulting disc would also help narrow this down.

I tried loading the coarse calibration parameters for the boundary calibration phase, and got a blank looking cd after the whole burning process. I also downloaded disc-probe but failed to launch it from the .bat file. I am using a pc I have with a fresh Windows on it so it might have some component missing, I just get no response or any window opening, with or without a CD in the drive. The drive is an HP SH-216DB. Discs are CD-R80 700MB by Silver Line. How the boundary calibration preview looks like: The result of burning the boundary calibration: And the result of the coarse calibration, which produced the numbers I used in the next step:

@YukaiP Thanks for the photos and the drive details, they help a lot.

The boundary disc in your photo looks unwritten to me. I can't see any of the target's rings on it. Wrong parameters would still leave rings, just in the wrong place, so this looks more like the burn never reached the disc. Your coarse disc does show its bands, so the drive can write these discs.

Two things would tell us which it is:
- Did DIS say the burn finished, with no error?
- What does the disc itself say? Once disc-probe runs, `python -m discprobe info --drive E` on that disc prints its status. `empty` means nothing was written. `complete` with around 359,846 sectors means it was written, and we're looking at a contrast or lighting problem instead.

Sorry about the launcher. My guess is that on a fresh Windows, `开始 Start.bat` tries Windows Terminal first, and if Terminal isn't set up yet it can fail without showing anything. Until I fix that, this skips Terminal:
1. Unzip the whole folder first. Running it from inside the zip won't work.
2. Open the folder in File Explorer, click the address bar, type `cmd` and press Enter.
3. In that window, type `python\shell.cmd` and press Enter.

If it shows an error, please paste it here.

Thanks for the support! Yep, DIS says the burn was completed, and refuses to even try to consider it a blank and attempt another burn. I went with your project, created an ISO, burned it, and got stuck at the timing check. I tried reducing the speed a couple of times until it reached the same verdict and suggested one that I already tried. I also tried 2x and 1x in case it helps but it didn't. I don't know much about optical drives so it's a reading & guessing game for me.

@YukaiP Sorry for the slow reply, and thanks for trying disc-probe and posting the output.

Your screenshot shows a bug on our side. For CDs, disc-probe only ever suggests 1411 or 2822, so it kept sending you back to speeds you had already tried. At those speeds your drive keeps a constant linear speed (CLV), and in that mode disc-probe can't work out where each sector sits on the disc.

Many drives only switch to a constant spin (CAV) at their higher CD speeds. Could you try these in order, and stop at the first one that says CAV?

```
python -m discprobe timing --drive E: --media cd --speed 4234
python -m discprobe timing --drive E: --media cd --speed 5645
python -m discprobe timing --drive E: --media cd --speed 7056
```

If all three still say CLV, your SH-216DB probably never spins a CD at a constant rate, and disc-probe can't measure CD geometry with it yet. I'm fixing the speed suggestions so they stop repeating, and looking into whether a CLV drive can still be used. I'll post an update here.

title: [功能请求] macOS 原生 GUI，并完整复用现有光盘预设 / 实测标定数据
body:
关联：#23、#46。本 Issue 补充 macOS GUI 的具体需求，重点是内置标定数据完整复用与导出参数一致性。

## 使用需求

希望 macOS 用户可以直接打开 `.app`，按照现有 Windows 版的“设计 → 预览 → 导出”流程生成光盘镜像，而无需手动填写 CLI 参数。界面可保留五项侧栏（设计、预览、导出、刻录、标定）和“图层 / 盘面画布 / 属性与影调”的三栏布局。

**App 必须附带已有的光盘预设与实测标定数据，并确保选择后实际用于镜像生成，不能只显示品牌名称，或只保留内外半径而丢失轨距与容量信息。**

## 数据来源与范围

参考版本：`df188fa7977703a028f153597216abca6c58988e`。建议统一使用仓库内的 [`src/DiscImageStudio.Core/Presets/built-in-disc-presets.json`](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/blob/df188fa7977703a028f153597216abca6c58988e/src/DiscImageStudio.Core/Presets/built-in-disc-presets.json)（schemaVersion 4），不要另外手工维护简化数值。该版本共 17 组：

| 介质 | 数量 | 预设 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CD | 4 | 标准 80min / 74min、铼德医疗水蓝盘、威宝 CD-R AZO 43438 |
| DVD | 8 | 标准 12cm / 8cm、威宝 DVD-R AZO 43533 / 43523、威宝 DVD+R AZO 43498、PHILIPS DVD+R、铼德 DVD+R / DVD-R E时代系列 |
| BD | 5 | 标准 25GB、铼德 BD-R 10x / 12x、威宝 BD-R 64099 / 64293 |

需要保留原始精度的内外半径、几何扇区数、可用扇区数、`pitchLinear` / `pitchQuadratic` / `pitchCubic`、BD 的 `invertMapping`，以及 ID、名称、说明、贡献者、资源键和兼容字段。UI 可缩短显示，但不能把显示精度重新写回。

例如 `ritek-dvd-r-e-series` 几何扇区数为 **2,298,496**，可用扇区数为 **2,297,888**，两者不可混用。威宝 DVD-R AZO 等预设的三次轨距系数也不能清零。

## 建议对接方式

1. 前端技术由维护者决定，光盘生成继续复用跨平台 Core / CD / DVD / BluRay / ImageIO 内核，避免重写物理编码算法。
2. 同一份内置 JSON 随 App 打包，离开源码目录、离线运行也可读取；避免只在开发环境依靠 SwiftPM 构建目录回退。
3. 新建工程按介质显示预设选择器，在设计、标定、导出页可查看所选品牌、说明、贡献者与实际参数。
4. 工程保存完整参数快照，避免预设库更新后改变已有工程结果；兼容缺少新字段的旧工程。
5. CD 生成传递 `sectors` / `usable-sectors`、内外半径和三次轨距；BD 传递 `total-sectors` / `usable-sectors`、内外半径、三次轨距与反转标志。
6. DVD 建议调用现有 `DvdImageGenerator.Generate(DvdImageRequest)` 和 `DvdStreamingOptions`，同时传递 `TotalSectors`、`UsableSectors`、内外半径和三次轨距。这样能复用 Windows 高层 API，保留纯绘图与随盘文件的容量边界。仅调用 `solve --image ... --iso-output ...` 不足以完成参数对接；现有 CLI 图像映射还需要显式几何参数。
7. macOS 发布包附带对应架构的自包含运行时，用户无需另装 .NET；保留 GPL 许可证与第三方声明。

## 本地原型与验证范围

本地已尝试 SwiftUI 前端，覆盖多图层导入与变换、亮度和抖动、设计投影、工程存储、随盘文件及镜像导出，并接入上述 17 组预设。DVD 增加了本地 CLI 适配入口以调用现有高层生成 API。

已通过 5 项 Swift 测试，覆盖全部预设加载、导出参数、快照保存/恢复、旧工程兼容、二值图像输出及非法参数；另完成 DVD 内核自检、小规模 CD WAV/CUE 输出，以及使用铼德 DVD-R E时代系列半径和三次轨距参数的 32 扇区 DVD 输出（65,536 字节）。本地 `.app` 构建与签名验证通过。

**尚未验证真实光驱刻录、实盘效果，以及所有介质的完整容量输出。本地原型源码尚未上传到此 Issue，不代表已有可直接拉取的 PR。** 此 Issue 先提供需求、数据来源与接口对接说明。

## 验收建议

- [ ] App 离开源码目录后仍能选择全部内置 CD / DVD / BD 预设。
- [ ] 完整保留标定精度、三次轨距系数、贡献者和容量边界。
- [ ] 保存并重开工程后，生成参数保持一致。
- [ ] DVD 输出容量使用可用扇区数，盘面映射保留原几何扇区数。
- [ ] 纯绘图与内圈 / 外圈随盘文件模式均正确使用预设。
- [ ] 区分设计投影预览和物理层读回模拟。
- [ ] Windows 即时刻录、照片辅助标定未移植时明确支持范围。
- [ ] 完成实盘验证后再声明与 Windows 版功能等价。

title: [Bug][DVD][v1.5.0] 随盘文件放在内圈或外圈均导致实盘图案扭曲，纯绘图正常
body:
使用 DiscImageStudio v1.5.0 制作 DVD 图案时发现的问题：

**纯图像模式下，使用实测标定参数可以正常成像；但只要添加随盘文件，无论文件放在内圈还是外圈，刻录后的实体盘面都会出现明显的整体图案扭曲。**

已经分别使用两张 DVD+R 测试内圈文件和外圈文件的情况，均出现扭曲。

同时，使用相同校准参数生成的精细标定十字线几乎没有扭曲，说明这套几何参数至少在纯标定图案模式下是有效的。

**English summary:** On v1.5.0, artwork-only DVD burns appear correctly aligned using measured calibration parameters. However, physical artwork becomes visibly warped when ordinary files are added, with either inner-ring or outer-ring placement. The ISO sidecar geometry is unchanged.

## 1. 测试环境

| 项目 | 信息 |
|---|---|
| 软件 | DiscImageStudio v1.5.0 |
| 系统 | Windows 11 |
| 刻录机 | ASUS BW-16D1HT |
| 固件 | 3.10 |
| 连接方式 | USB |
| 介质 | SONY DVD+R Ver.1.3，4.7GB，1×–16× |
| MID | `SONY-D21-00` |
| 内圈刻码 | `DRP5GG0001` |
| 刻录方式 | ISO 导出后刻录（具体软件及两次写入速度待确认） |

### 使用的实测几何参数

```text
totalSectors:   2295104
usableSectors:  2295104
innerRadiusMm:  23.933879893109697
outerRadiusMm:  57.957884267199745

pitchLinear:     3.0133964007494058E-05
pitchQuadratic: -7.447423575670042E-05
pitchCubic:      5.376838738985465E-05

channelBitLengthNm: 133.3
```

这些参数来自三阶段辅助标定后的用户预设。

## 2. 复现步骤

1. 新建 DVD 工程，选择上述实测标定预设。
2. 导入一张人物图片，保持相同图层位置和影调设置。
3. 不添加随盘文件，生成纯绘图 ISO 并刻录。实盘图案正常。
4. 复制该工程，在「随盘文件」中添加文件夹，位置选择「内圈」，重新生成混合 ISO 并刻录。实盘图案扭曲。
5. 将随盘文件位置改为「外圈」，再次生成混合 ISO，使用另一张空白 DVD+R 刻录。实盘图案同样扭曲。
6. 对照 ISO 元数据及软件预览，发现纯绘图与内圈文件版本的 `imageMapping` 完全一致，预览中未出现对应的整体扭曲。

### 已完成的实盘对照

| 模式 | 文件位置 | 实盘效果 |
|---|---|---|
| 纯绘图 | 无文件 | 正常 |
| 精细标定图案 | 无文件 | 十字线接近笔直 |
| 图案 + 普通文件 | 内圈 | 整体扭曲 |
| 图案 + 普通文件 | 外圈 | 整体扭曲 |

## 3. 预期行为

添加随盘文件后，软件应当保留原有整盘几何映射，只改变文件占用区及可绘制的 LBA 区间。

在未被文件占用的绘图区内，相同图片和相同几何参数应生成位置一致的图案，不应出现额外的整体旋转、螺旋扭曲或非线性变形。

## 4. 实际行为

两种文件布局的实盘图案均发生明显扭曲，而纯图像模式以及精细标定图案正常。

这不是简单的文件占用导致内圈或外圈部分图片缺失，而是剩余绘图区内的人物轮廓也发生了变形。

### 实拍对照

（此处插入纯绘图成品、内圈文件成品、外圈文件成品和精细标定盘照片。）

## 5. ISO 元数据对照

已生成并对比：

- `si.iso.json`：带内圈文件
- `si-nodata.iso.json`：纯绘图

两份 JSON 中的 `imageMapping` 对象逐字段完全一致，包含相同的五项几何参数、图片映射半径与影调参数。

共同的生成设置：

```text
algorithm: dispersion
fastOutput: true
exactEccEfmReplay: false
readCompatibility: off

tone.ditherStrength: 0.907728706624626
tone.brightness: 6.056782334384589
tone.srgbLinearization: false
```

内圈文件版本：

```text
mode: hybrid-iso9660-joliet
fileCount: 5
fileBytes: 43615740
dataEndLbaExclusive: 21325
startLba: 21328
fillSectors: 2273776
```

纯绘图版本：

```text
mode: raw-sector-image
startLba: 0
fillSectors: 2295104
```
希望能够确认这是特定介质、刻录机的兼容性问题，还是 DVD 混合盘生成路径的问题。感谢开发者的工作！

nodes.body:
经过检查，我们认为我们的算法没有出现问题。社区也有不少成功案例分享出来。
因此，问题更可能发生在生成之后的刻录或读取链路，而不是 ISO 的数据生成阶段。
个人认为可能是您光驱存在独特的写入策略。这个 issue 一直开着吧，看看是否有更多类似的反馈。

title: CMC CD-R (97m26s66f): only concentric circles visible, radial lines and large areas completely smeared
body: [calibration-861546d4.calibration.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34641717/calibration-861546d4.calibration.json) [test black white.wav.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34641738/test.black.white.wav.json) Disc Image Studio (Windows), standard 80 min CD preset. Media: CMC Magnetics CD-R 80 (ATIP 97m26s66f, lead-out 79:59:71), tested with three labels (no-name, Tevion, Platinum), all the same result. Burned as WAV+CUE in DAO with ImgBurn, and with the built-in live burner. Calibration target (r 24.5 / 56.8 mm, 359,846 sectors, 1200 mm/s): concentric circles are clearly visible at the expected radii, but the radial cross lines are not visible anywhere. Half-black/half-white test image (r 24.84 / 58.02 mm, 1200 mm/s): disc looks completely uniform, no spiral arms at all. So the radial mapping seems roughly right, but the angular drift seems to be hundreds of turns. Related to #249 (CMC DVD-R)? Is there a recommended way to get a first coarse estimate for this media? Photos and calibration JSON attached.

title: Two-level drawing shows no visible contrast on a slim USB drive (LG GSA-T50L) — CD and DVD
body:
**摘要（中文）**：在轻薄 USB 刻录机 `HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GSA-T50L`（固件 SC04）上，无论 CD-R 还是 DVD-R，按官方流程生成的盘面图案在数据面上都看不到可见对比。已排除介质、速度、字节值范围等因素，数据本身写入正确（回读校验通过）。附带反馈一个该驱动下「即时刻录」稳定失败的问题（0xC0AA0301）。想请教：这是轻薄刻录机写策略的已知限制，还是我们漏了什么？

---

## Environment

- App: Disc Image Studio v1.3.6 (win-x64 portable), Windows 11
- Drive: `HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GSA-T50L`, USB, slim, firmware `SC04`, letter `D:`
- Media A: CD-R `97m15s17f`, Panasonic/Ritek (printable, white matte top), 359 843 sectors
- Media B: DVD-R `CMC MAG. AM3`, 2 297 888 sectors

## What was produced

**CD (two-level `0x0D / 0xAA`)**
`cd-generate --sectors 359800 --inner 24.5 --outer 56.8 --tone-dither 0 --interleave true`
Burned at 10x and again at 16x (ImgBurn, SPTI/SAO, no truncation). Read-back verified: only `0x0D` and `0xAA` present, 48 wedges reconstructed, 98.6% area match to the design.

**CD (byte-value sweep, custom track)**
Since the palette is hard-coded (`TwoLevelPalette = [0x0D, 0xAA]`), I generated the track myself using the app's own `CddaInterleaveTable` delay compensation (verified by inverting the app's output back to the source image) with 8 angular zones of 45°: `0x00, 0x0D, 0x10, 0x21, 0x28, 0x63, 0xAA, 0xFF`. Burned at 10x (359 800 sectors).

**DVD (maximum-contrast two-level test)**
`solve --iso-output ... --total-sectors 2297888 --fill-sectors 2297888 --fast-output true --generated-inner-radius-mm 23.991460627731737 --generated-outer-radius-mm 57.964893657925366` with the measured cubic pitch coefficients of the `verbatim-dvd-r-azo-43533` preset. Image: left half pure black, right half pure white, plus a thin black outer ring, a checkerboard patch and two letters. `payload-transition-class-error=0`. Burned with ImgBurn at 4x (DAO), 2 297 888 sectors, completed without errors.

## Observed

- On the **data side** of the CD-R, the recorded/unrecorded boundary and the lead-out area are clearly visible — so the medium and drive do produce a visible mark/land-density difference at that scale.
- Inside the recorded area, however, no visible difference: the two-level image is invisible under a point light at any angle.
- Photo analysis of the CD (angular FFT of the gray level in the data annulus) gives an 8-fold (i.e. 45°-zone) amplitude of **~1.8% of full scale** — at the noise floor of the illumination gradient.
- Photo analysis of the DVD (36 angular bins, 50–86% radius) shows no half-disc step: variation is entirely explained by the specular/diffraction fans.
- The diffusion fans themselves are very prominent on this drive (sharp-edged diffraction wedges), they just do not follow the drawn texture.

## Questions

1. Is this an expected limitation of slim notebook-class drives (write-strategy equalisation of mark/land density), or should a two-level drawing normally be visible on this class of hardware?
2. Is there any media type or byte pairing that gives a measurably larger visible contrast than `0x0D/0xAA` on CD? I could not find a configurable palette; if the 2-level pair is fixed by design, that answers it.
3. Would a full-size 5.25" drive plausibly change the result, before I spend money on one?

## Secondary issue: streaming burn always fails on this drive

`Start streaming burn` fails immediately on this drive, before any data is written (disc stays blank, `NextWritableAddress = 0`):

```
正在写入 CD 导入区…
Streaming burn failed: Windows 刻录接口在"写入 CD DAO 音轨"时返回错误 0xC0AA0301
```

The log also shows the requested `10x` being overridden: `设备设置速度=24× (设备返回的设置值)`.

Same cue burned through ImgBurn over SPTI works fine on 10x/16x (avg 8.9x/12.6x, BURN-Proof enabled, `Operation Successfully Completed`). Possibly the IMAPI2 raw CD-DAO path is rejected by this drive; a note about the fallback (export + external burner) might be worth adding to the docs.

Happy to run further tests on this hardware if anything specific would help.

title: DVD-R burn fails within the first ~8000 sectors (Focus/Tracking Servo error) on LG GSA-T50N – normal data DVDs burn fine
body:
**Setup**
- DiscImageStudio v1.5.0 (win-x64), Windows 11
- Drive: HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GSA-T50N, firmware RF07, external USB enclosure (connected directly to a USB 3.0 port)
- Media: Verbatim DVD-R AZO 16x (pack code 43729), MID: MCC 03RG20
- Preset: Verbatim DVD-R AZO (43533) (measured)
- Burned with ImgBurn 2.5.8.0, "Write image file to disc", verify off

**Problem**
Every drawing ISO fails very early in the burn with a hardware error from the drive:

| Attempt | Speed | DVD read compatibility | Failed at sectors | Error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4x | off | 7584–7615 | Tracking Servo Failure |
| 2 | 8x | off | 3040–3071 | Focus Servo Error |
| 3 | 8x | on | 8064–8095 | Focus Servo Error |

Sense data (attempt 3): 70 00 04 00 00 00 00 0A 32 34 04 0C 09 02 00 00 00 00 (Hardware Error, ASC/ASCQ 09/02).
Retries never succeed. The failures happen in the first ~1 mm of the recorded area, where the design is plain white background.

**What works**
- A normal data DVD-R (2.6 GB of video files, ISO9660+UDF) from the same pack burns at 8x and verifies with 0 retries, so the drive and the media are fine.
- The same drive burns CD-R drawing tracks (WAV+CUE) without errors.

So it looks like the drawing data itself makes this drive lose focus/tracking on DVD-R. Is there a setting or data mode that is more tolerant for older drives? Happy to test builds or send logs.

title: [Enhancement] 基于盘面质量检测的粗标定和边界标定二合一替代方案（CD / DVD / BD）
body: 肉眼和常规拍摄设备分辨率过低，注意到光驱本身就是对光盘盘面良好而精确的读取设备，提出如下方法： **_目前主要可且仅可用于：完全代替粗标定和边界标定_** **_通过一次刻录即可实现 100% 精确\* 的半径确定_** _\* 100% 精确：误差 <300nm、小于 DVD 最短记录点长度_ 准备工作 1. 一张空白待刻录光盘 2. **一台具备 C1 C2 (CD) 或 PIE PIF (DVD) 或 LDC BIS (BD) 错误汇报能力的光驱\*\*** 3. 适当的刻录和测试软件，如 QPxTool，需具备详细报告导出功能 _\*\* 可通过 QPxTool 等工具检查光驱功能_ 流程（进行了简单的测试、主要以 DVD 为例，其它未经测试、原理相同理论可行、实际操作可能需要调整）： 1. 从任意预设参数开始、直接制作**精细标定图案**的镜像 ISO 并刻录 3. 使用适当的笔（**严禁在笔迹未干、可流动或盘面有异常突起时进行下一步操作**）在光盘盘面（**激光头读写面，或即背面**）上画一条或数条径向线段进行人为污染、粗细至少 1mm 4. 使用适当的测试软件，对光驱进行 Error Correction（或称 盘面质量 等）测试、保存原始格式结果文件 4. 根据标定生成的 ISO 镜像文件、笔迹的大致几何形状和上一步得到的详细测试结果，可得到三者接近扇区级别的对应关系并进行计算（例如在盘面上沿半径方向画线段之后，由于画线痕迹污染了盘面、使得资料信息读回时发生错误，即可从详细的 PIF 结果和标定镜像得到标定图案和光盘轨道参数的对应关系）（直接交给 AI 吧） 个人测试结果： 设备：威宝 DVD-R 43523 + 华硕 SDRW-08U9M-U 1. 直接使用软件内精细标定图案生成标定 ISO 并刻录 2. 画一条约 1mm 宽的径向墨线，贯穿已刻录区域 3. 使用 QPxTool 执行质量测试，保存 .qpx 文件 4. 结合原始 ISO 和错误统计进行拟合，先保存拟合结果，再与 DIS 内置的同型号光盘参数比较 本方案原始拟合数据和修正数据^ 模拟如下（^请注意 +6 修正数据是经过和现成数据比对得到的、只有参考价值没有实际应用意义） 使用精细标定图案 左：不设置任何参数；中：跟随本方案流程后直接得到的结果；右：仅供参考 +6 扇区修正^ 结果 | 项目 | 本方案 | +6 修正^ 后 | _软件内现成预设_ | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 内半径 mm | 23.991200974 | 23.991352495 | 23.991460628 | | 外半径 mm | 57.935869104 | 57.935931849 | 57.935788281 | | 一次轨距系数 | -6.192262×10⁻⁵ | -6.192248×10⁻⁵ | -3.922322×10⁻⁵ | | 二次轨距系数 | -2.515432×10⁻⁶ | -2.514498×10⁻⁶ | +6.952867×10⁻⁵ | | 三次轨距系数 | +6.877196×10⁻⁵ | +6.877142×10⁻⁵ | -4.658924×10⁻⁵ | | 角度差 RMS | 11.31° | 1.42° | 0 | | 跨半径相位变化幅度 | 47.50° | 7.80° | 0 | | 最大图案位置差 | 15.34mm | 3.50mm | 0 | 改进方向（应能获得更好结果）： 1. 在画线污染前先进行一轮光盘的盘面质量 / 错误测试，用 污染前后测试结果数据的差值 代替污染后单方面测试结果 2. 更精准地画线 3. 基于理论计算调整画线粗细，避免线宽和扇区长度之比过小造成误差 4. 使用相对夹角已知的多条画线代替单条半径或直径画线

title: Boundary Calibration fails validation despite hundreds of carefully placed points
body: I'm having trouble getting a valid result from Boundary Calibration. I carefully place points along the visible physical boundary on the calibration image. The number of points does not seem to solve the problem: I've tried both ~200 and over 450 points. The predicted boundary matches the manually marked points quite well near the inner radius, but progressively deviates toward the outer radius. If I place points starting from the outer edge and work toward the center, the opposite happens: the prediction matches the outer region but deviates toward the center. In other words, the prediction seems unable to match the entire boundary simultaneously. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Burn a Boundary Calibration target to a DVD+RW. 2. Take a photograph of the disc and load it into Boundary Calibration. 3. Carefully mark the visible boundary across the entire radial range. 4. Run the calibration. 5. Observe that the predicted boundary deviates progressively from the marked points in one part of the disc. 6. Try changing the distribution of marked points. The region where the prediction matches changes accordingly, but the full boundary still cannot be fitted. ## Error message With 423 manually placed points, the application reports: ``` [18:58:04] Calibration: Calculating parameters using all 423 curve points… [18:58:15] Calibration: Automatic validation did not pass. All 423 points and parameter candidates are preserved. Candidates can be applied after confirming the photographed match. The boundary segments do not match a single disc model. Check for misplaced points, photo rectification errors, or segments crossing another boundary. Candidates with different winding counts still fit these segments. Trace a longer, clear boundary at another radius and calculate again. ``` ## Expected behavior I would expect the calibration algorithm to use all marked points to find the best-fitting disc model, or clearly indicate which points or boundary segments are inconsistent with the model. ## Hardware and media - Drive: Pioneer DVR-218L - Firmware: 1.02 - Media: DVD+RW - Write speed: 4x - Application: DiscImageStudio v1.5.0+29b8cc1177c67a16b1ee5d2eb1a8c122f01cad17

title: Fine Calibration Issue
body: # Fine Calibration: predicted curve deviates significantly from manually traced boundary and marks valid points as outliers ## Description During Fine Calibration, the predicted curve can significantly deviate from the manually traced boundary, even when the boundary is clearly visible and has been carefully traced with a large number of points. In my test, I traced a highly irregular but clearly visible boundary using approximately 158 points. The points closely follow the actual photographed boundary, including its local bends and irregularities. However, the predicted curve does not follow the traced points. Instead, it appears excessively smoothed and deviates significantly from the actual trace, particularly near the inner and outer parts of the recording area. As a result, correctly placed points are highlighted as outliers, and the calibration reports very large errors. ## Observed results In the attached screenshot: - 158 points are retained. - `Fit cubic track pitch` is enabled. - Mean error: 1.399 mm. - Maximum error: 4.869 mm. - The predicted curve visibly diverges from the manually traced boundary. - Several correctly placed points are classified as large deviations. The actual boundary is clearly visible in the photograph and can be traced accurately. The discrepancy is between the traced points and the mathematical prediction, not necessarily the point placement. ## Expected behavior The fitting process should make effective use of all available traced points. In particular: 1. The predicted curve should represent the traced boundary as accurately as the selected mathematical model allows. 2. A large number of manually placed points should meaningfully constrain the fit. 3. The fitting process should not excessively smooth away local variations in the traced boundary. 4. Points should not be classified as outliers merely because the fitted model cannot reproduce local variations. 5. The application should make it possible to distinguish genuine tracing mistakes from limitations of the fitting model. It would also be useful to have an option to display the raw traced path without smoothing, alongside the fitted mathematical curve. ## Possible cause The fitting model may be too restrictive to represent the actual radial variation of the recorded track. The enabled cubic track pitch model uses a limited number of coefficients. It may be unable to reproduce local variations in the photographed boundary, causing the fitted curve to compromise between different radial regions. It is also worth investigating whether the fitting or visualization pipeline applies excessive smoothing or downsampling to the original points. ## Environment - DiscImageStudio v1.5.0 - Windows 10 x64 - Drive: Pioneer DVR-218L - Media: DVD+RW - Calibration stage: Fine Calibration - Traced points: approximately 158 - Cubic track pitch fitting: enabled

title: Two-level pattern invisible on a desktop drive (LG GH22NS40): recorded area uniform, only the recorded/unrecorded boundary visible — CD-R and DVD-R
body:
**摘要（中文）**：在台式 5.25 英寸刻录机 `HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GH22NS40` 上，CD-R 与 DVD-R 的双层图案均不可见。已排除速度（4×/16×）、介质批次与工具链：回读数据正确，**刻录区与未刻录区的边界清晰可见**，但刻录区内部没有任何图案。径向特征（同心环、刻录边界）可见，角向特征（半黑半白、文字、十字线）完全均匀。症状与 #292 / #242 / #295 一致，但本机是**台式机光驱**，不是薄型 USB 光驱。

---

## Environment

- **App**: DiscImageStudio CLI `v1.3.6` (`DiscImageStudio-CLI-v1.3.6-linux-x64.tar.gz`, SHA256 verified against the release `SHA256SUMS.txt`), self-contained, run on Arch Linux (kernel 7.2.8).
- **Drive**: `HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GH22NS40`, firmware `NL02`, SATA, **5.25" desktop drive** (serial `K5XA4J82909`). Reports MMC-2/3, DVD-R/-RW/-RAM, DVD+R/+RW, CD-R/RW, SAO/DAO, test write.
- **Burn tools**: `growisofs` (dvd+rw-tools) for DVD, `cdrecord 3.02a09` (cdrtools) `-dao` for CD. The app's Windows in-app burner is not used — this is the documented "export image + external burner" path.
- **Media**:
  - DVD-R 16× (generic, no MID read out), capacity 2 297 888 sectors.
  - CD-R 52× 700 MB (Multilaser). `cdrecord -atip` reports lead-in 97:27:18, lead-out 79:59:74 (359 849 sectors), "Medium Type B, low Beta category (B-)", short strategy type / phthalocyanine.

## What was produced

All images via the Linux CLI, then burned externally at the stated speed.

1. **CD-DA art, full disc** (concentric rings + large text), `cd-generate --sectors 359849`, burned `cdrecord dev=/dev/sr0 -dao speed=8 -audio` (and 4×, and 32× with a half-black/half-white image).
2. **DVD calibration card** (10 tone rings, solid black wedge, radial spokes, outer dashed band), `solve --total-sectors 2296437 --fill-sectors 2296416 --inner-radius-mm 24 --outer-radius-mm 58.04 --tone-dither 0.99`, burned `growisofs -Z ... -speed=4 -dvd-compat`.
3. **DVD text art** (`DISC` 175 pt, `2026` 100 pt, two smaller lines, thin ring), `--tone-dither 0`, burned at 4× and again at 16×.
4. **DVD radial half-fill** (only the inner half of the sectors written), `--fill-sectors 1148208`, burned at 4×.
5. **DVD angular half-black / half-white** (left half white, right half black), `--tone-dither 0`, burned at 16×.

Every burn completed with exit code 0 and no errors; every disc was closed and is readable.

## Observed

- **CD-R (all three speeds)**: data reads back correctly (`cdda2wav` returns the exact track length; the app reconstructs the art from the read-back WAV). On the disc, nothing but a ~1 mm ring near the hub; the rest of the data area is visually unchanged. Read-back shows ~12–14 % of samples muted to `0x00`, i.e. a marginal but readable burn.
- **DVD calibration card (4×)**: the ten tone rings look visible to a casual look, **but photo analysis of the data annulus gives a smooth monotonic radial profile** (116 → 200 → 160 across r = 100…340 px) with no ~20 px periodicity, and the solid black wedge region measures 158 — the *brightest* area of the disc. So the rings were most likely the generic diffraction of the data spiral, not the card.
- **DVD text art (4× and 16×)**: only a thin ring near the outer edge is visible; no letters at either speed.
- **DVD radial half-fill (4×)**: a **clear circular boundary** is visible at ~44 mm, exactly where the written region ends. This proves the drive and media do produce a visible mark/land-density difference at that scale.
- **DVD angular half-black/half-white (16×)**: the disc looks **uniformly burned** — no straight boundary, no spiral, no half-disc step.

## What this rules out

- **Speed**: 4× and 16× on DVD, 4×/8×/32× on CD — identical result.
- **Media batch**: two different media types (CD-R and DVD-R), different dyes, different wavelengths.
- **Toolchain / data correctness**: the app's own `simulate` reconstructs every image from the generated ISO, and the burned discs read back correctly.
- **Missing mark**: the recorded/unrecorded boundary is clearly visible, so the laser does modify the dye.
- **Rendering side / viewing angle**: verified under a point light at several angles; the uniform area stays uniform.
- **Wrong polarity**: the innermost calibration ring reads dark, i.e. the black level does render darker where it renders at all.

## Question

Issue #295 asks whether this is an expected limitation of **slim notebook-class drives** (write-strategy equalisation of mark/land density). This report is the same symptom on a **full-size 5.25" desktop drive**, which I believe has not been reported before, so it may narrow the cause:

1. Is this a known write-strategy equalisation behaviour that can affect desktop drives too, or is there a parameter we are missing?
2. Is there any media/drive combination known to work with this drive family (LG GH22NS40 / Renesas chipset)?
3. Would a different drive model be expected to change the result, before buying one?

Happy to run further tests on this exact hardware — the drive is available and the discs are sacrificial.

nodes.body:
## Second drive tested — same result

I swapped the drive and repeated the exact same experiment.

- **Drive B**: `HL-DT-ST DVD-RAM GH22NS30`, firmware `2.00`, SATA, also a **5.25" desktop drive** (same HLDS family, one generation older than the GH22NS40).
- **Image**: identical `angular.iso` (left half pure white, right half pure black, `--tone-dither 0`, 2 296 416 sectors, r0 24 / r1 58.04 mm).
- **Burn**: `growisofs -Z /dev/sr0=angular.iso -speed=16 -dvd-compat` → exit 0, 16.0×, no errors, disc closed.

**Result: identical.** The disc looks uniformly burned — no straight boundary, no spiral, no half-disc step. Same as the GH22NS40 at 16×.

So this is not one specific drive model: two different HLDS drives (2008 and 2009 generations, different firmware) behave the same, on two different DVD-R batches.

## A pattern in the existing reports

Every report of this symptom I could find involves a **Hitachi-LG Data Storage** drive:

| Issue | Drive |
| --- | --- |
| this one | `HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GH22NS40` (desktop) |
| this one | `HL-DT-ST DVD-RAM GH22NS30` (desktop) |
| #295 | `HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GSA-T50L` (slim USB) |
| #242 | `LG HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GSA-H66N` (desktop) |
| #185 | `Transcend TS8XDVDS-K` (slim USB — these are usually HLDS OEM) |

That suggests the limiting factor may be the **HLDS write strategy**, which appears to equalise mark/land density inside the recorded area: the recorded/unrecorded boundary and the lead-out remain clearly visible, while the two-level pattern does not.

## Test that would settle it

A burn of the same ISO on a **non-HLDS drive** (Pioneer, ASUS, Lite-On, Plextor, or an older NEC/Optiarc). If the pattern appears there, the cause is confirmed as HLDS write strategy and the project could document a "known incompatible drive family" note. If it also fails on non-HLDS hardware, then the cause is broader than the drive family.

I still have both drives and sacrificial media and can run any further test you suggest.

## Following the HLDS hypothesis — next test planned

Both drives I tested report `HL-DT-ST` in INQUIRY, i.e. they are **Hitachi-LG Data Storage** units. Since every other report of this symptom also comes from HLDS hardware (#295 `GSA-T50L`, #242 `GSA-H66N`, #185 Transcend slim — very likely HLDS OEM), I am going to test the same ISO on a **non-HLDS** drive.

For anyone else following this, the INQUIRY vendor string tells you the real manufacturer, independent of the retail brand:

| INQUIRY vendor | Manufacturer | Expected to work? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HL-DT-ST` | HLDS (Hitachi-LG) | ❌ what failed in all reports so far |
| `TSSTcorp` | Toshiba-Samsung | untested |
| `PLDS` / `ATAPI` / `LITE-ON` | Lite-On | untested |
| `PIONEER` | Pioneer | untested |
| `Optiarc` / `SONY` | Sony-NEC | untested |
| `ASUS`, `LG`, `Verbatim`, `Teac`, `BenQ` | rebadged — may be any of the above | check the model |

Check with:

```bash
cdrecord -checkdrive dev=/dev/sr0 | grep -E 'Vendor_info|Identifikation'
```

## Test plan

1. Install a non-HLDS desktop drive (**Samsung SH-224DB**, `TSSTcorp`, is the cheapest and most common option here).
2. Verify the INQUIRY vendor string is not `HL-DT-ST`.
3. Burn the **same** `angular.iso` (left half white / right half black, `--tone-dither 0`, 2 296 416 sectors, r0 24 / r1 58.04 mm) with the same command: `growisofs -Z /dev/sr0=angular.iso -speed=16 -dvd-compat`.
4. Report whether the boundary is a straight diameter, a spiral, or absent.

I will post the result here, including photos, so the HLDS hypothesis is either confirmed or refuted with hardware evidence.

If the maintainer has a specific drive family or firmware known to produce visible two-level art, that would save a purchase — otherwise I will report back with the TSST result.

## The pattern *is* written — it is rotated. Geometry sweep results

Following the earlier comments, I found a way to separate "no contrast" from "wrong geometry": the half-black/half-white image does show structure if you look closely — but the dividing line arrives as a **spiral**, not as a straight diameter. So the two-level pattern is being recorded; it is rotated by an angular error that accumulates with radius.

That makes the drift measurable: the distance between consecutive turns of that spiral is the drift per revolution.

### Method

Same image (`angular.png`, left half pure white / right half pure black), same command, same drive (`GH22NS30`), same media, `--tone-dither 0`, burned at 16×. Only `--outer-radius-mm` changes, always with `--total-sectors 2297888` (the disc's own `Track Size`) and `--fill-sectors 2297824`.

Ring count is measured over the **first 10 mm** from the inner data edge, with a steel rule laid on the disc.

| `--outer-radius-mm` | rings per 10 mm | implied spacing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 58.040 | 18 | 0.56 mm |
| 58.008 | 16 | 0.63 mm |
| **57.800** | **6** | **1.67 mm** |

Photos of the first two measurements (rule in frame, same disc surface):

![r1 = 58.040 — 18 rings per 10 mm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ghpo/discimagestudio-evidence/main/midia-1medicao.jpg)

![r1 = 58.008 — 16 rings per 10 mm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ghpo/discimagestudio-evidence/main/midia-2medicao.jpg)

### The part that does not fit

At `r1 = 57.800` the first centimetre improves a lot (18 → 6 rings), **but the spacing keeps shrinking with radius**: after that first centimetre the rings become progressively finer until there are more than 70 of them and a phone camera can no longer resolve them.

For a constant pitch error the spacing would be **constant** across the radius. For a linear pitch coefficient (`--pitch-linear a1`) it would vary smoothly. Fitting the observed 5–10× change in spacing to `pitch(r) = p0 (1 + a1 x)` requires `a1 ≈ -5`, i.e. a negative track pitch — physically impossible.

So the residual is **not** a radius or pitch error that the documented parameters can express. What remains is the mapping between sector number and physical angle: the model assumes the ideal CLV relationship, and this drive appears to deviate from it in a way that varies with radius.

### Questions

1. Is there any CLI parameter (or a value the GUI's fine calibration produces) that compensates for a sector→angle mapping deviation rather than a radius/pitch deviation?
2. Does the GUI's spoke calibration measure exactly this — and would its result be usable from the CLI via `--pitch-*`? If so, which coefficient carries the angular term?
3. If this is a known drive limitation, is there a list of drives known to work? Both drives here are HLDS (`GH22NS40`, `GH22NS30`), consistent with the pattern noted earlier.

For completeness: with the unmodified preset geometry (`--total-sectors 2296437`, `r1 = 58.04`) the same image produced a disc that looked completely uniform, and the drift only became visible as a measurable spiral after switching to the disc's real sector count. That step alone may be worth documenting.

Happy to run more experiments — both drives and sacrificial media are still available. A flatbed scan of the disc is also possible if that would help quantify the spacing profile.

title: Parameter contribution: Verbatim DVD+RW 4x 4.7 GB (94839)
body:
## Disc and setup

I would like to share my current calibration settings for **Verbatim DVD+RW 4.7 GB / 4x, product 94839**, for others using the same product and for consideration as a disc preset.

- Product: [Verbatim DVD+RW, Amazon ASIN B0001LRPE2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0001LRPE2)
- Recorder: HL-DT-ST DVDRAM GUE0N, firmware T.02, USB
- Write speed: 4x
- Burning method: exported ISO written through Windows IMAPI2 with DVD+RW overwrite enabled
- Device-reported capacity: 2,295,104 sectors
- Media ID (MID): not confirmed

## Parameters

The radii and three pitch coefficients below preserve the full values from my current settings.

```json
{
  "id": "verbatim-dvd-plus-rw-4x-94839",

  "description": "User-contributed settings for Verbatim DVD+RW 4.7 GB 4x, product 94839; verify against the exact media and batch.",
  "totalSectors": 2295104,
  "usableSectors": 2295104,
  "innerRadiusMm": 23.98021495351053,
  "outerRadiusMm": 57.99222803078272,
  "channelBitLengthNm": 133.3,
  "pitchLinear": -3.9256854319227684E-05,
  "pitchQuadratic": 6.964795915429256E-05,
  "pitchCubic": -4.670918950137523E-05
}
```

## Validation scope

The three pitch coefficients are unchanged from the starting preset used during this calibration; they are not being presented as an independently measured pitch profile for product 94839.
